summary: Defines and registers the value grouptextchat for the URI purpose element of the SIP Conference Event Package. This lets conference servers advertise such services.

eli5.summary: A new label meaning this address is for group text chat.

subtitle: A new purpose value for conference chat room URIs in SIP.

tldr.problem: SIP conferences advertise auxiliary services (web pages, recordings) via purpose-labeled URIs, but had no standard way to advertise a text chat room for the conference.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7106 registers the value "grouptextchat" as a valid purpose in the SIP Conference Event Package, letting servers advertise chat rooms alongside other conference resources.
tldr.outcome: Conference systems can now inform participants about group chat in a standardized way, supporting any chat technology (XMPP, IRC, MSRP, web-based) via the appropriate URI scheme.

today: RFC 7106 standardizes a registry value for conference chat URIs. It remains the normative definition of the "grouptextchat" purpose in the SIP Parameters registry, allowing conference servers and clients to interoperate when advertising group text chat capabilities.

sections.title: Conferences and Auxiliary Services
sections.content:
The Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) and its Conference Event Package allow a conference server to advertise information about an ongoing conference: the subject, the participants, the media being used, recordings, web pages, and other auxiliary services.

These services are listed in <service-uris> as <entry> elements. Each entry contains a URI and a <purpose> element that identifies what the URI is for. Existing purposes include "web-page" for additional information, "participation-uri" for joining the conference, and others. However, there was no standard purpose for advertising a text chat room associated with the conference.
sections.eli5: Video conferences advertise web pages, recordings, and ways to join. They were missing a way to say "here is the text chat."

sections.title: The grouptextchat Purpose
sections.content:
RFC 7106 adds the "grouptextchat" purpose to the SIP URI Purposes registry. When a conference server includes an entry with this purpose, the URI points to a text chat facility for the conference participants.

The actual URI can be any suitable scheme: sip: or sips: for SIP-signaled MSRP-based chat, xmpp: for XMPP Multi-User Chat (MUC), irc: for Internet Relay Chat, or http:/https: for web-based chat. The purpose label tells the client "join here for group text chat"; the scheme in the URI tells it how.
sections.eli5: The new label says "this is a text chat room." The actual URI can point to any kind of chat service.

sections.title: Use Cases and Features
sections.content:
A text chat room can enhance an audio or video conference by allowing side conversations, questions, or coordinated action. Some systems use group chat to manage roles and permissions: moderators can mute, kick out, or ban participants in the chat, and the conference software can mirror these actions in the audio/video call.

A server might advertise a single chat room, multiple chat rooms (e.g., separate channels for different languages or subtopics), or reuse the same URI for both the conference focus and the chat service. When multiple chat rooms are advertised, clients can present them as separate options or join them all; there is no requirement to synchronize content between them.
sections.eli5: Chat rooms can be used for questions, private side talk, or for organizers to control who participates in the call.

sections.title: Security Concerns
sections.content:
If an attacker can modify conference notifications in transit, they can trick participants into joining an attacker-controlled chat room instead of the legitimate one. Participants would then expose their messages to eavesdropping and could be impersonated.

The RFC recommends the same protections already suggested for conference URIs: use SIP security mechanisms like S/MIME or TLS to protect notification messages. When those are unavailable, clients should clearly display the target chat URI so users can notice tampering. Advanced clients can also enforce policies, such as requiring the chat room to be in the same administrative domain as the conference, or refusing to auto-join without user approval when the conference is large.
sections.eli5: Attackers might trick you into joining a fake chat room. Showing the address clearly helps users spot this.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content:
RFC 7106 registers "grouptextchat" in the IANA "URI Purposes" sub-registry under "Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) Parameters". The registration includes the value, a description of what it means, and a reference to this RFC.

This registration ensures that the value is reserved and that implementers can rely on it having a standard meaning across different SIP implementations.
sections.eli5: The name "grouptextchat" is officially registered, so all SIP software will understand it the same way.
